outcomes.text: Explain the main ideas in Coordination and supplementation.
Recognise the patterns in real sentences.
Use the ideas when you read and write.

key_terms.definition: A non-headed construction joining two or more elements of equal syntactic status.
One member of a coordination, equal in status to the other members.
A linking word such as and, or or but that marks a coordinate.
The coordinate without its coordinator or modifying material.
A coordinate including its coordinator and any modifiers.
A coordination with two coordinates.
A coordination with more than two coordinates.
Coordination overtly marked by a coordinator.
Coordination not marked by a coordinator.
Multiple coordination with a coordinator before the final coordinate only.
Multiple coordination with a coordinator before every non-initial coordinate.
Coordination with paired markers such as both ... and or either ... or.
A coordination in which a coordination functions as a coordinate within a larger one.
Coordination of clauses.
Coordination of phrases or words within a clause.
A coordination interpreted as a single joint entity, as in Kim and Pat are a couple.
Coordination in which material is omitted from one coordinate under identity with another.
Coordination of expressions that are not independent constituents but form matching right-hand sequences.
Coordination in which a shared right constituent follows both coordinates.
Coordination in which the second coordinate is attached at the end of the clause.
An adverb such as however or therefore that links clauses or sentences.
The relation between an anchor and a detached supplement.
A prosodically detached expression related to an anchor without being integrated as a dependent.
The expression or situation that a supplement relates to.
A supplement that characterises or identifies an anchor, as in my friend, a doctor.
A supplement commenting on or qualifying the clause, often an interpolation.
A construction in which an NP is placed outside the main clause and resumed by a pronoun.
A sequence that functions as a constituent only for the purposes of a particular coordination.

opening.prompt: Why is Kim and Pat a non-headed construction?

options.text: The coordinates are equal and neither is head or dependent.

options.feedback: Only the final coordinate is marked.

options.text: A detached expression related to an anchor
A coordinate of a non-headed construction
A complement licensed by a verb
Coordination with material omitted from one coordinate
options.feedback: Kim is an engineer and Pat a barrister.
Either is the initial correlative; or marks the following coordinate.

closing.prompt: Why does Kim, Tom and Pat, and your parents require layering?

options.text: The medial coordinates are not marked uniformly.
options.feedback: A single-layer multiple coordination must treat medial coordinates alike.

closing.prompt: Why is Hurry up or we’ll be late not a simple free choice?

options.feedback: The second coordinate gives the result of not hurrying.

closing.prompt: Why can this afternoon and on Tuesday be coordinated?

options.text: They share the same adjunct function despite different categories.

closing.prompt: Why is most of them exhausted a supplement in The tourists – most of them exhausted – got into the bus?

options.text: It is detached from the clause and relates to the tourists as an anchor.
options.feedback: It is not a dependent of got.

options.text: It is a complement of got.

closing.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes coordination from supplementation?

options.text: Coordination joins equal coordinates; supplementation relates a detached expression to an anchor.
options.feedback: Coordination is integrated; supplementation is detached.
